text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An accord on financial cooperation. Spain received Prime Minister Hariri and expressed concern about stumbling peace talks.
- Iraq postpones visit by business delegation to Lebanon. Beirut had refused to allow Iraqi athletes to participate in the Pan Arab Games.
- Israeli air raid and wide-scale shelling of south Lebanon. Two civilian martyrs and the monitoring committee to meet tomorrow.
- Investigating judge Mirza issue indictment demanding imprisonment of labour leaders Elias Abou Rizk and Yasser Nehme for "defaming Lebanon's reputation".
- Treasury bills auction raises 284.5 billion Lebanese pounds. Subsrciption strongest on the two-year bills.
- Foreign Minister Faris Bouez signs $100,000 deal with U.N. Interim Forces in Lebanon.
- Leader of Lebanon's "hunger revolt" former chief of Hizbollah Sheikh Tufaili says: Our movement will continue and the storm has not ended.
- Commander of UNIFIL troops says Israel has breached the terms of a 1996 understanding that bars it from hitting civilian targets.
